01

Tick

AI planner that finds time for you

RoleUI/UX Designer
PlatformWeb app
VersionRedesign 2.0
tick.app/today

The problem. Calendars tell you what’s booked. They don’t help you decide where new things should go, and “AI scheduling” can feel scary if you can’t see what it did.

What I changed. In the redesign, AI always asks first. Suggestions come with a reason and an accept or skip button, events it placed get a small AI tag, and you decide where it’s allowed to plan by painting your free hours.

02

Loop

Async check-ins for remote teams

RoleUI/UX Designer
PlatformWeb app · English
TypeConcept
getloop.app/

Why I made it. Remote teams spread across time zones end up with a daily standup that’s at 9am for some people and midnight for others. Most of it could have been a message.

The idea. Each person writes a two-minute check-in in their own morning. The team reads it whenever they start. Blockers stand out so someone can jump in, and when a live call really is needed, Loop shows the hours when everyone is awake.

#F6F4EE
#1C2620
#C9F06B
#1F7A52
#FF7A59
Two-minute check-insYesterday, today, blockers and a mood
Time-zone overlap finderEveryone’s hours on one 24-hour strip
Blockers that get seenHighlighted, with a one-tap “I can help”
03

KiBehtar

Price comparison & smart shopping

RoleUI/UX Designer
PlatformWeb
VersionRedesign 2.0
kibehtar.com/

The problem. When you want to buy something, you just want to know where it’s cheapest and whether now is a good time to buy. Most comparison sites hide that answer under ads and noise.

What I changed. The redesign puts that answer first: stores sorted by price, the cheapest one highlighted, a price history chart, and alerts for when a product hits your price. For people who don’t know what to buy yet, there’s a chat-style shopping advisor.

04

Vira

Play-centre management & customer loyalty

RoleUI/UX Designer
PlatformWeb dashboard
VersionRedesign 2.0
panel.vira.app/dashboard

The problem. Front-desk staff at a busy kids’ play centre juggle timers, payments and loyalty points at once. The first version showed everything as plain tables, so urgent things (a child whose time is up) didn’t stand out.

My redesign. I rebuilt the panel around one question: who needs attention right now? Play timers use colour to show status, checkout became a single clear receipt, and the loyalty club got levels, progress and rewards so it feels worth joining.

#2F6BFF

One-step checkoutReceipt, discount, points and payment in one modal
Loyalty club with levelsSilver, gold and diamond tiers with rewards to redeem
05

Masalebaz

Daily maths & physics practice for teens

RoleUI/UX Designer
PlatformMobile app
TypeConcept
π √x F = ma ∑

Why I made it. I teach maths and physics, and I keep seeing the same thing: students don’t hate the subject, they hate feeling stuck. Long practice sheets make that worse.

The idea. One short set a day, friendly feedback after every answer, and a streak to come back for. A playful mascot and warm colours make it feel like a game rather than homework.

About

A bit about me

I’m a computer engineer who fell for design. I care about the small stuff: a button that says exactly what it does, a screen that doesn’t make you think twice.

When I’m not in Figma, I’m usually teaching maths or physics, or making posts for a social media page I run. I’m comfortable with remote work: clear written updates, async feedback and a lot of Figma comments.
